**Finding: compliant (at fallback).**

Clause 4(h) is a mutual assignment provision that already contains the carve-out we need for AP — assignment without consent to an affiliate, to a purchaser of all or substantially all relevant assets, or to a successor by merger, stock sale or consolidation — with all other assignments subject to consent not to be unreasonably withheld. There is no change-of-control trigger anywhere in the agreement, so Kubient has no termination, consent or re-pricing right on an AP change of control (the termination provisions in 4(a)–(b) are limited to convenience after the Initial Term, material breach and insolvency).

Because the carve-out runs to both parties, this sits at the playbook fallback rather than the preferred position. The only gaps from preferred are the lack of a written-notice requirement and the absence of an express bar on Kubient assigning to an AP competitor — minor sub-elements, noted but not redlined.
